samples.summary: `expect(() => sheet.toDisplayString(...)).not.toThrow()` is vacuous — toDisplayString is async so it can never throw synchronously
samples.evidence: `Sheet.toDisplayString` is declared `async toDisplayString(ref: Ref): Promise<string>` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:967). Any error inside it (including the RangeError from Intl this test claims to guard against) becomes a rejected promise, never a synchronous throw, so `.not.toThrow()` passes unconditionally — it would pass even with clamping removed entirely. It also leaves a floating/unawaited promise. The line should be `await expect(sheet.toDisplayString(...)).resolves.toBe(formatValue('1.5','number',20))`. (The preceding `dp === 20` assertion in the same test is meaningful; only this line is fake coverage.)

samples.summary: Clamp tests compare formatValue against formatValue, so they hold for any clamp function including a constant one
samples.evidence: `expect(formatValue('1.5','number',400,...)).toBe(formatValue('1.5','number',20,...))` and the -3/0 and NaN/2 pairs both run through the same `clampDecimals` (format.ts:182). If clampDecimals were replaced with `() => 2`, all three pairs would still be equal ('1.50' === '1.50') and the test passes. Nothing pins the clamp to 20, to 0, or to the fallback 2 against an independent oracle. The same self-referential shape appears in decimals.test.ts:536 (`toBe(formatValue('1.5','number',20))`). A literal expectation (e.g. '1.50000000000000000000' for 20, '2' for 0) would actually distinguish the behavior.

verdict.reason: Verified both halves of the claim in the repo. decimals.test.ts:527 contains `expect(() => sheet.toDisplayString({ r: 1, c: 1 })).not.toThrow()`, and sheet.ts:967 declares `async toDisplayString(ref: Ref): Promise<string>`. An async function converts internal errors (e.g. the Intl RangeError this test claims to guard) into a rejected promise, so the synchronous invocation cannot throw and `.not.toThrow()` passes unconditionally — it would pass with clamping removed. This is a vacuous assertion presented as coverage for the clamping behavior, squarely in the test-adequacy lane; the correct form (`await expect(...).resolves.toBe(...)`) is used in the adjacent test at lines 530-539, which does not rescue line 527 since it exercises a stored dp:400 rather than the changeDecimals-clamped dp:20 path. No refutation ground applies: code is present as described, the line executes in an active it() block, and it is in-lane.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. format.test.ts:140-150 ("should clamp a decimal count Intl would reject") compares formatValue against formatValue for all three pairs (400 vs 20, -3 vs 0, NaN vs 2), and every one of those six calls routes through the same clampDecimals at format.ts:182. Replacing clampDecimals (format.ts:22-30, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES=20 at format.ts:14) with a constant `() => 2` yields '1.50' on both sides of every pair, so the test still passes — the bounds 20, 0 and the fallback 2 are not pinned by any independent oracle. A repo-wide grep for clampDecimals/MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES/literal 1.50000 finds only implementation sites, so no test anywhere asserts the clamp targets literally; neighbouring tests in the same file (format.test.ts:24-32) do use literal oracles, showing this shape is a departure. decimals.test.ts:536-538 repeats the same self-referential shape (toBe(formatValue('1.5','number',20)) for a stored dp of 400), and the sibling at decimals.test.ts:519-528 only asserts not.toThrow(). The test retains only the weak power to detect total clamp removal (which would fall into safeFormat's catch at format.ts:45-59); it cannot distinguish the actual clamp behavior it is named for. Real and blocking under the test-adequacy rubric as a vacuous test presented as coverage for a new hostile-input behavior.
